title: Buttons in a Collector’s Tin
description: Sort a collection of clothing buttons through their shapes, attachment methods, and decorative materials.
cardDescription: Sort a collection of clothing buttons through their shapes, attachment methods, and decorative materials.
focus: A button can be attached through face holes or through a projecting shank. The clues distinguish that fastening structure from the button’s material and the container storing it.
solvingTip: Use the attachment method before the material or shape word.
words: Projecting loop on the back of a button for sewing it on
Long narrow fastening piece passed through a loop
Early synthetic resin used for some collectible buttons
Mother-of-___, iridescent shell material used in buttons
Flat round shape of many shirt buttons
Small garment fastener collected in this tin
Opening through which sewing thread can pass
Fine strand attaching a button to cloth
Metal container holding the small collection
Backing on which a matched set of buttons may be mounted
Curved opening receiving a toggle fastener
Measurement distinguishing a coat button from a tiny shirt one
Hue used to group the collector's finds
Outer edge of a circular button

answerNotes.SHANK: A shank provides an attachment below the button face; another design uses holes through the face itself.
answerNotes.TOGGLE: A toggle has a barlike shape rather than the flat disk form of many buttons.
answerNotes.BAKELITE: Bakelite is a material name associated with phenolic resin; not every old plastic button is made from it.
answerNotes.PEARL: Mother-of-pearl is shell material rather than a round loose pearl gemstone.
answerNotes.DISC: Disc describes shape, while the shank or holes describe the attachment arrangement.

title: A Family Glass Vase
description: Look at a familiar glass vase through its shape, colors, rim, and place in a family cabinet.
cardDescription: Look at a familiar glass vase through its shape, colors, rim, and place in a family cabinet.
focus: The vase holds flowers, while its base supports it on a shelf. The clues use visible features rather than glassmaking terminology.
solvingTip: Start with a color or a short part of the vase.
words: Top edge around the vase's opening
Bottom part supporting the vase upright
Golden-brown color seen in some glass vases
Flower stalk standing in the vase
Hard material from which this clear vase is made
Cut bloom displayed in the container
Flat support beneath the family display

Leaf-like color of some colored glass
Easy to see through, as an uncolored vase may be

Liquid supplied to the cut flower stems

answerNotes.VASE: A vase holds cut stems and water rather than soil and growing roots.
answerNotes.RIM: The rim surrounds the opening rather than supporting the vessel underneath.
answerNotes.BASE: The base is the supporting bottom rather than the upper opening.
answerNotes.AMBER: Amber names a color here rather than the material from which the vase is made.
answerNotes.STEM: A cut stem reaches into the water while the blossom stays above the opening.

title: A Music Box on the Shelf
description: Explore a mechanical music box through its pinned cylinder, tuned teeth, and winding mechanism.
cardDescription: Explore a mechanical music box through its pinned cylinder, tuned teeth, and winding mechanism.
subtheme: A Music Box on the Shelf
focus: In a familiar cylinder music box, projecting pins pluck tuned metal teeth. The clues distinguish the part carrying the pattern from the comb producing the notes.
solvingTip: Use the source of motion or sound to identify each component.
words: Pinned rotating drum carrying a tune pattern in one music-box design
Row of tuned metal teeth plucked inside a music box

answerNotes.CYLINDER: A cylinder carries the arrangement; other music boxes use interchangeable disks instead.
answerNotes.COMB: The comb produces notes when its teeth vibrate; it is not a grooming tool in this scene.
answerNotes.PIN: A pin triggers a note at a position in the tune pattern.
answerNotes.GOVERNOR: A governor helps control the speed, while the spring supplies the stored energy.
answerNotes.SPRING: The spring powers the mechanism as it unwinds rather than generating new energy while running.

title: Shells Collected at the Beach
description: Sort a small beach collection through familiar shell names, shapes, colors, and textures.
cardDescription: Sort a small beach collection through familiar shell names, shapes, colors, and textures.
focus: Some shells have two matching halves, while a snail's shell is commonly one coiled piece.
solvingTip: Use the shape and texture clues before the animal names.

answerNotes.SHELL: An empty shell once protected an animal's body.
answerNotes.CLAM: A clam's shell has two parts joined along a hinge.
answerNotes.SNAIL: Many familiar snails have a spiral shell, though shell shapes vary.
answerNotes.SPIRAL: A spiral winds around a central point rather than forming straight rows.
answerNotes.PAIR: Pair counts the two pieces rather than naming the animal.

answerNotes.WATCH: A pocket watch is carried rather than worn on a wrist.
